intent.raw_query: Eastern Europe city hop Prague + Budapest, $1200, 8 days, September 2026

experiences.name: Prague Castle Complex Exploration
experiences.description: Spend a half-day exploring the largest ancient castle complex in the world, including St. Vitus Cathedral, the Old Royal Palace, and Golden Lane. Wander through centuries of Bohemian history with stunning panoramic views over the red-roofed city below.

experiences.name: Budapest Thermal Bath Experience at Széchenyi
experiences.description: Soak in one of Europe's largest and most iconic thermal bath complexes, built in 1913 in stunning Neo-Baroque style. Experience the unique Hungarian bathing culture that has been central to Budapest life for centuries, with multiple indoor and outdoor pools at varying temperatures.

experiences.name: Prague Old Town & Astronomical Clock Walking Tour
experiences.description: Join a guided walking tour through the medieval Old Town Square, witness the famous 15th-century Orloj Astronomical Clock chime on the hour, explore the Jewish Quarter (Josefov), and discover hidden Gothic and Baroque architecture at every turn.

experiences.name: Budapest Danube River Evening Cruise
experiences.description: Board a scenic evening cruise along the Danube River to witness the breathtaking illuminated skyline of Budapest, including the UNESCO-listed Parliament Building, Buda Castle, and the Chain Bridge. A quintessential way to appreciate the city's architectural grandeur from the water.

experiences.name: Budapest Ruin Bar Crawl & Local Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore Budapest's legendary ruin bars born in the Jewish Quarter, starting with the iconic Szimpla Kert. Combine the crawl with tastings of Hungarian street food including lángos (fried dough), kürtőskalács (chimney cake), and local craft beers for an authentic cultural night out.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Eastern Europe (Prague + Budapest)
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Prague Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Use this time to rest on the plane.
day_by_day.afternoon: After landing, take the Airport Express Bus (Line AE) to Náměstí Republiky, then connect via tram to Hradčany district (~60 CZK total). Check in to Prague Boutique Stay. Once settled, take a gentle orientation walk around Hradčany — stroll past Prague Castle's outer walls, admire St. Vitus Cathedral exterior, and explore the charming Nový Svět (New World) cobblestone lane nearby.
day_by_day.evening: Walk down to Malá Strana (Lesser Town) via the castle steps. Enjoy the golden-hour views of the city from the castle ramparts (free from outside). Grab dinner in Malá Strana and then return to the hotel on foot or by tram.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or grab a snack at the airport
meals.lunch: Pick up a fresh trdelník or sandwich from a bakery near Hradčany upon arrival (~80–120 CZK)
meals.dinner: Lokál Malá Strana — a beloved Czech pub offering affordable schnitzel, svíčková (beef sirloin in cream sauce), and draft Pilsner Urquell (~200–280 CZK per person)

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — you just landed. Get your bearings, pick up a transit pass (24-hour pass ~120 CZK or 3-day pass ~330 CZK from the airport), and rest well for the busy days ahead. September weather in Prague is mild (15–20°C), so pack a light jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Full Prague Castle Complex visit — buy a Circuit B ticket (~250 CZK) covering St. Vitus Cathedral interior, Old Royal Palace, and St. George's Basilica. Arrive early (9:00) to beat crowds. Spend 2–3 hours exploring the Gothic grandeur of the cathedral and the medieval palace halls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk across the iconic Charles Bridge (free), admiring the 30 Baroque statues. Continue into Old Town (Staré Město). Visit the Old Town Square to see the famous Astronomical Clock (Orloj) strike the hour. Explore the Jewish Quarter (Josefov) from the outside — peek at the Old Jewish Cemetery through the gates (entry ~350 CZK if budget allows, or admire from outside for free). Browse the vibrant market stalls.
day_by_day.evening: Catch a classical music concert at one of Prague's affordable evening performances — St. Nicholas Church in Old Town frequently hosts budget-friendly concerts (~350–500 CZK). Alternatively, enjoy a free organ recital at St. Vitus if scheduled. Return to Hradčany via tram.

meals.breakfast: Café Louvre-style corner bakery near the hotel — grab a croissant and coffee (~80–100 CZK)
meals.lunch: Nase Maso butcher shop in Old Town — outstanding open-faced sandwiches and meatballs (~120–160 CZK)
meals.dinner: U Zlatého Tygra — legendary Prague pub with Pilsner Urquell on tap and hearty Czech dishes like goulash with bread dumplings (~180–250 CZK)

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — today covers significant ground. The Charles Bridge is most atmospheric in early morning or evening. Prague Castle is a UNESCO World Heritage Site — the views over the red-roofed city are spectacular in September light.

day_by_day.morning: Take tram to Vinohrady or Žižkov districts — explore Prague's bohemian, local neighborhoods away from tourist crowds. Visit the striking Žižkov Television Tower (entry ~250 CZK) for panoramic city views, with its famous crawling baby sculptures by David Černý. Wander the Art Nouveau residential streets of Vinohrady.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Vyšehrad Fortress (free entry to grounds) — Prague's lesser-known but historically rich fortress offering sweeping Vltava River views. Explore the Vyšehrad Cemetery where Czech luminaries like Dvořák and Smetana are buried (free). Walk the fortress walls and enjoy the peaceful gardens — a true local gem.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the city center and explore Wenceslas Square (Václavské náměstí) — the grand boulevard at the heart of Czech modern history. Browse the evening atmosphere, then head to a local pivnice (pub) in Nové Město for a relaxed dinner.

meals.breakfast: Café Savoy near Malá Strana — elegant but affordable breakfast with pastries and coffee (~150–200 CZK)
meals.lunch: Piknik food market at Náměstí Míru in Vinohrady — rotating local vendors with excellent value meals (~100–150 CZK)
meals.dinner: Pivovarský Klub — craft beer pub in Žižkov with rotating Czech microbrews and affordable pub food like roasted pork knee (~220–300 CZK)

day_by_day.notes: Vyšehrad is often overlooked by tourists — enjoy the tranquility. The Žižkov area has a gritty, authentic Prague character with more bars per capita than almost anywhere in Europe. September evenings can be cool — bring that jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at leisure in Hradčany — visit the Strahov Monastery and its extraordinary Baroque library halls (~150 CZK entry). The theological and philosophical halls are among the most beautiful library rooms in Europe. Browse the monastery's small art gallery and enjoy the panoramic garden terrace overlooking Prague.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel to Letná Park (free) — a vast hilltop park beloved by locals. Rent a bike (~200–300 CZK for 2 hours) or walk the tree-lined paths. Visit the famous Letná Beer Garden (Letenský zámeček) for an affordable Czech beer with arguably the best view of Prague's bridges and Old Town rooftops. This is a quintessential local Prague experience.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Holešovice district — Prague's up-and-coming creative hub. Visit DOX Centre for Contemporary Art (~180 CZK) if open, or browse the street art and independent shops. Have dinner at one of Holešovice's trendy but affordable eateries before returning to Hradčany.

meals.breakfast: Grab fresh bread, cheese, and fruit from Hradčany's local Billa supermarket — assemble a budget picnic breakfast (~60–80 CZK)
meals.lunch: Letenský zámeček Beer Garden — Czech sausages, open-faced sandwiches, and cold beer with a view (~120–180 CZK)
meals.dinner: Eska in Holešovice — modern Czech cuisine using fermented and local ingredients at surprisingly reasonable prices (~250–350 CZK)

day_by_day.notes: Today is your last full day in Prague before moving to Budapest tomorrow. Pack your bags tonight and confirm your overnight bus or train booking to Budapest. RegioJet and FlixBus offer Prague–Budapest routes from ~€15–25, departing from Florenc Bus Terminal or Praha hlavní nádraží (main train station).

day_by_day.morning: Early checkout from Prague Boutique Stay. Take tram or metro to the departure point for your Prague–Budapest transport. If taking an overnight bus (recommended budget option — ~8 hours, from €15), you may have departed late Friday night and arrive in Budapest this morning. If taking a daytime train (~7 hours, from €20 on RegioJet), depart around 8:00–9:00 from Praha hlavní nádraží.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Budapest (Keleti or Kelenföld station). Check in to your Budapest accommodation (budget hostels in the 7th District/Jewish Quarter like Maverick City Lodge or Retox Party Hostel offer dorms from €12–18/night or private rooms from €35–50). Drop bags and take a first walk through the lively 7th District (Erzsébetváros) — Budapest's ruin bar district.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the legendary ruin bars of Budapest — start with Szimpla Kert, the original ruin bar, a sprawling multi-room complex in a repurposed derelict building. Sip affordable Hungarian pálinka (fruit brandy) or local Dreher beer. Soak in the eclectic, artistic atmosphere — this is quintessential Budapest nightlife.

meals.breakfast: Pack snacks from Prague for the journey — train station grab-and-go items (~100–150 CZK / ~600–900 HUF)
meals.lunch: On the train/bus — bring packed food or purchase from RegioJet's onboard bistro (~€5–8)
meals.dinner: Karavan Street Food Court near Szimpla Kert — outdoor food trucks serving langos (Hungarian fried dough with toppings), burgers, and more (~1,500–2,500 HUF / €4–7)

day_by_day.notes: Currency changes today — Hungary uses Hungarian Forint (HUF). As of 2027, approximately €1 ≈ 380–400 HUF. Withdraw HUF from ATMs (avoid airport exchange booths). Budapest is significantly cheaper than Prague. The 7th District is the best base for budget travelers — central, vibrant, and full of affordable food and drink options.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Hungarian Parliament Building (Országház) — one of the world's most beautiful parliament buildings, situated majestically on the Danube bank. Book the English guided tour in advance (~6,000 HUF / ~€15 for non-EU citizens, free for EU citizens with ID). The neo-Gothic interior with the Hungarian Crown Jewels is extraordinary. Afterward, walk along the Danube Promenade (Duna-korzó) on the Pest side.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the iconic Chain Bridge (Széchenyi Lánchíd) on foot to the Buda side. Hike up to Buda Castle (Budavári Palota) — the funicular costs ~1,400 HUF but walking up Castle Hill is free and rewarding. Explore the Hungarian National Gallery (within the castle, ~3,200 HUF) or simply wander the castle district's medieval streets and Fisherman's Bastion (Halászbástya) — the fairy-tale neo-Romanesque terraces offer stunning panoramic views of the Danube and Pest (free access to outer terraces).
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from Fisherman's Bastion or Gellért Hill (free — hike up for 20 minutes for the best panoramic view in Budapest). Descend to the Buda side riverbank and enjoy dinner in a local étterem (Hungarian restaurant) before crossing back to Pest.

meals.breakfast: Café Gerbeaud in Vörösmarty Square — a Budapest institution; have a coffee and rétes (strudel) (~1,800–2,500 HUF)
meals.lunch: Hungarikum Bisztró near the Parliament — authentic Hungarian goulash soup and főzelék (vegetable stew) at local prices (~2,000–3,000 HUF)
meals.dinner: Menza Restaurant in the 6th District — retro-style Hungarian canteen with generous portions of pörkölt (pork stew) and lángos (~2,500–3,500 HUF)

day_by_day.notes: Fisherman's Bastion is magical at sunset in September — arrive 30–45 minutes before dusk. Gellért Hill is a steeper but free alternative with equally stunning views. Sunday in Budapest is lively — markets and locals fill the parks and promenades.

day_by_day.morning: Spend a classic Budapest morning at Széchenyi Thermal Baths (Széchenyi Gyógyfürdő) — the largest medicinal bath complex in Europe, housed in a stunning Neo-Baroque palace in City Park. A basic cabin ticket costs ~7,500–9,000 HUF (~€19–23). Soak in the outdoor pools, try the steam rooms, and experience this uniquely Hungarian wellness tradition. Arrive by 9:00 to avoid weekend crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore City Park (Városliget) — free and beautiful. Visit Heroes' Square (Hősök tere), Budapest's grandest public square featuring the Millennium Monument with statues of Hungarian chieftains and kings. Walk through the park to Vajdahunyad Castle (exterior free, museum inside ~2,000 HUF) — a whimsical castle built for the 1896 millennium exhibition combining Romanesque, Gothic, and Baroque styles.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Great Market Hall (Nagycsarnok) — Budapest's magnificent 19th-century iron-and-brick market hall. Browse the ground floor for fresh Hungarian produce, paprika, salami, and local cheeses. The upper floor has affordable lángos stalls — perfect for a budget dinner. Afterward, stroll the vibrant Váci Street and the Inner City for evening atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Grab a kürtőskalács (chimney cake) and coffee from a stand near your accommodation (~600–900 HUF)
meals.lunch: Light snack at Széchenyi Baths café or pack your own — sandwiches from a local pékség (bakery) (~800–1,200 HUF)
meals.dinner: Great Market Hall upper floor — classic lángos with sour cream and cheese (~800–1,200 HUF) plus a glass of Hungarian wine (~600–900 HUF)

day_by_day.notes: Bring a swimsuit, flip-flops, and a small towel for the thermal baths (or rent towels onsite for ~1,000 HUF). The baths are a non-negotiable Budapest experience. City Park is undergoing renovation in phases but Heroes' Square and Vajdahunyad remain fully accessible.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Great Synagogue on Dohány Street (Dohány utcai zsinagóga) — the largest synagogue in Europe and the second largest in the world, a breathtaking Moorish-Byzantine masterpiece. Entry includes the Hungarian Jewish Museum and the moving Holocaust Memorial Garden (~5,000 HUF). This is a profound historical and cultural experience. Explore the surrounding Jewish Quarter on foot.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final afternoon in Budapest — visit the Hungarian State Opera House (Magyar Állami Operaház) for a guided architectural tour (~3,500 HUF) of one of Europe's most opulent opera buildings, or simply admire the exterior on Andrássy Avenue. Walk the grand Andrássy Avenue (a UNESCO World Heritage boulevard) toward Vörösmarty Square. Do last-minute souvenir shopping — pick up Hungarian paprika, Tokaji wine, and Unicum liqueur at the Great Market Hall or local shops.
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner in Budapest — splurge slightly on your last night. Head to a traditional Hungarian restaurant for a memorable farewell meal. Afterward, take one final walk along the illuminated Danube riverbank — the Chain Bridge, Parliament, and Buda Castle lit up at night is one of Europe's most spectacular urban views. Head to the airport or your departure point.

meals.breakfast: Auguszt Cukrászda patisserie — a Budapest institution since 1870, offering exquisite pastries and coffee (~1,500–2,000 HUF)
meals.lunch: Frici Papa Kifőzdéje — a beloved Budapest canteen serving traditional Hungarian home-cooking (főzelék, stews, soups) at rock-bottom prices (~1,500–2,000 HUF)
meals.dinner: Borkonyha Winekitchen or Klassz Wine Bar — Hungarian wines paired with modern Hungarian cuisine for a special farewell meal (~4,000–6,000 HUF per person, a worthwhile splurge)

day_by_day.notes: Budapest Liszt Ferenc Airport is ~30 minutes from the city center. Take the 100E airport bus (~900 HUF one-way) — avoid expensive taxis. Allow 2.5–3 hours before your flight. This final evening Danube walk is unmissable — the Budapest night panorama is a UNESCO World Heritage Site in its own right. End your Eastern European adventure on a high note!

trip_options.title: Classic Eastern Europe (Prague + Budapest) Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives at 13:00. Travel from airport to Hradčany district hotel (approx. 30–40 min by taxi or Airport Express bus + metro). Check in, freshen up, and get oriented.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle neighborhood orientation walk around Hradčany. Stroll through the historic Hradčany Square (Hradčanské náměstí), admire the Archbishop's Palace facade, and walk along the castle walls for sweeping panoramic views of Prague's red-roofed skyline. Visit the nearby Loreta Shrine courtyard for a quick atmospheric introduction to the area.
day_by_day.evening: Walk down Nerudova Street — one of Prague's most picturesque cobblestone lanes — to the Lesser Town (Malá Strana). Cross the iconic Charles Bridge at dusk for golden-hour views. Settle into the Malá Strana neighborhood for dinner and a relaxing first evening.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in transit
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite after check-in at a local café near the hotel, such as a traditional Czech open-faced sandwich (chlebíček) from a neighborhood bakery or deli — budget ~5–8 EUR
meals.dinner: Café Savoy (Malá Strana) — elegant yet mid-range Art Nouveau brasserie with classic Czech dishes like svíčková (beef sirloin in cream sauce) and fresh pastries. Budget ~20–28 EUR per person.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Focus on soaking in the atmosphere rather than ticking off sights. Pick up a transit card at the airport or nearest metro station for easy city travel.

day_by_day.morning: Full Prague Castle Complex exploration. Start early (gates open at 6:00, ticket offices at 9:00) to beat the crowds. Visit St. Vitus Cathedral, the Old Royal Palace, St. George's Basilica, and walk the famous Golden Lane — a row of tiny colorful medieval houses once inhabited by alchemists and castle guards.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend from the castle through the charming Malá Strana district. Visit the Baroque Wallenstein Garden (free entry), then cross Charles Bridge and explore the Old Town (Staré Město). Visit the Old Town Square, watch the Astronomical Clock (Orloj) chime on the hour, and wander through the Jewish Quarter (Josefov) — admire the exterior of the Old Jewish Cemetery and synagogues.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the vibrant Old Town Square atmosphere as evening falls. Browse the surrounding streets and enjoy a traditional Czech dinner nearby.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or nearby café in Hradčany — try a Czech-style breakfast with rye bread, cheese, and cold cuts. Budget ~6–10 EUR.
meals.lunch: Lokál Malá Strana — beloved local pub-restaurant serving fresh Pilsner Urquell on tap and hearty Czech classics like goulash with bread dumplings. Budget ~12–16 EUR per person.
meals.dinner: Mincovna Restaurant on Old Town Square — solid Czech and European cuisine with a great terrace view of the square. Budget ~18–25 EUR per person.

day_by_day.notes: Prague Castle is one of the largest castle complexes in the world — wear comfortable shoes. The combined ticket for all castle buildings costs around 250 CZK (~10 EUR). Book online to skip queues.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Museum of Medieval Art at the Convent of St. Agnes of Bohemia — a stunning Gothic complex housing Bohemian and Central European art from the 13th–16th centuries. Then explore the Vltava riverbank and Náplavka embankment, a beloved local promenade.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the funicular up Petřín Hill for panoramic views of Prague. Visit the Petřín Lookout Tower (a mini Eiffel Tower lookalike) and the Mirror Maze. Descend through the rose gardens. In the late afternoon, visit the Mucha Museum in the New Town — dedicated to the Art Nouveau master Alfons Mucha, a Czech national treasure.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Vinohrady neighborhood — one of Prague's most livable and stylish districts — for dinner and a relaxed evening walk around Náměstí Míru square and its Neo-Gothic church.

meals.breakfast: Café Louvre (New Town) — a historic Prague café dating to 1902, beloved by Franz Kafka and Albert Einstein. Great eggs, pastries, and coffee. Budget ~8–12 EUR.
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch from a Náplavka farmers' market stall (open Saturdays, but nearby delis work on weekdays) or a quick bite at a Petřín Hill café. Budget ~8–12 EUR.
meals.dinner: Eska (Žižkov/Karlín area, short tram ride) — a celebrated modern Czech restaurant championing local, seasonal ingredients with a creative twist. Budget ~22–30 EUR per person.

day_by_day.notes: Petřín funicular runs every 10–15 minutes and is covered by a standard Prague transit ticket. September weather in Prague is typically mild (15–20°C) — a light jacket is recommended for evenings.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Kutná Hora — a UNESCO World Heritage town 1.5 hours from Prague by train. Visit the hauntingly beautiful Sedlec Ossuary (Bone Church), where the bones of 40,000–70,000 people are arranged into elaborate decorations, including a chandelier containing every bone in the human body.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk into the town center of Kutná Hora and visit the stunning Gothic Cathedral of St. Barbara — a masterpiece rivaling St. Vitus in Prague. Stroll through the charming medieval town square and the Italian Court (Vlašský dvůr), once a royal mint.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Prague by train (last trains run until late evening). Arrive back in Prague for a relaxed dinner in the Malá Strana or Hradčany area, close to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at the hotel before an early departure, or grab a pastry and coffee at Prague hlavní nádraží (main train station). Budget ~5–8 EUR.
meals.lunch: Dačický Restaurant in Kutná Hora — a historic inn serving traditional Bohemian cuisine in a medieval setting. Try the roast duck or wild boar. Budget ~12–18 EUR per person.
meals.dinner: U Zlaté Studně (The Golden Well) hotel restaurant in Malá Strana — a romantic terrace restaurant with breathtaking Prague views. Slightly splurge-worthy for a special evening. Budget ~30–40 EUR per person.

day_by_day.notes: Trains from Prague hlavní nádraží to Kutná Hora run regularly; round-trip costs ~6–8 EUR. The Ossuary is in Sedlec, a 15-min walk or short bus ride from the main train station — plan accordingly. Book Ossuary tickets online.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Prague to Budapest. Take a morning train (RegioJet or Railjet — scenic and comfortable, ~6.5–7 hours) or a budget flight (~1 hour). Trains depart Prague hlavní nádraží; book in advance for best prices (~20–40 EUR). Enjoy the Central European countryside scenery en route.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Budapest (Keleti or Kelenföld station). Check into your Budapest accommodation. Take a gentle orientation walk along the Danube riverbank — the UNESCO-listed panorama of the Parliament building, Chain Bridge, and Buda Castle is breathtaking, especially in afternoon light.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the lively Great Market Hall (Nagycsarnok) if still open (closes 18:00 on Saturdays) for a taste of Hungarian produce and souvenirs. Then head to the vibrant Ruin Bar district in the Jewish Quarter — start the evening at Szimpla Kert, Budapest's most famous ruin bar, for a drink and to soak in the eclectic atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast at Prague station or on the train (RegioJet has a bistro car). Budget ~6–10 EUR.
meals.lunch: Lunch on the train or at a Budapest station café upon arrival. Budget ~8–12 EUR.
meals.dinner: Borkonyha (Wine Kitchen) — a Michelin-starred but surprisingly accessible restaurant near the Hungarian Parliament, offering modern Hungarian cuisine with an outstanding wine list. Budget ~30–40 EUR per person. Alternatively, try Kárpátia for a more traditional grand Budapest dining experience at ~20–28 EUR.

day_by_day.notes: Book train tickets well in advance (especially RegioJet) for the best prices and seat reservations. If flying, factor in airport transfer time on both ends. Store luggage at the Budapest hotel before exploring if check-in isn't available yet.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Buda Castle District. Take the historic Castle Hill Funicular (Budavári Sikló) up from the Chain Bridge. Visit the Royal Palace complex, now home to the Hungarian National Gallery (outstanding collection of Hungarian fine art). Walk through the Fisherman's Bastion — a fairy-tale Neo-Romanesque terrace with iconic views across the Danube to the Parliament.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Matthias Church (Mátyás-templom) — a stunning Gothic-Baroque church with a magnificent diamond-pattern tiled roof. Descend to the Pest side via the Chain Bridge on foot — a classic Budapest experience. Explore the elegant Andrássy Avenue, a UNESCO-listed Champs-Élysées-style boulevard, and visit the Hungarian State Opera House (exterior or guided tour at 15:00 or 16:00).
day_by_day.evening: Treat yourself to a traditional Hungarian thermal bath experience at Széchenyi Baths — the largest medicinal bath complex in Europe, set in a stunning Neo-Baroque palace in City Park. Evening bathing (after 18:00) is less crowded and atmospheric under the lights.

meals.breakfast: New York Café breakfast — one of the world's most beautiful cafés, a Budapest institution since 1894. Ornate frescoed ceilings and excellent pastries. Budget ~12–18 EUR.
meals.lunch: Hungarikum Bisztró near Buda Castle — authentic Hungarian home cooking with classics like chicken paprikash, stuffed cabbage, and lángos. Budget ~12–18 EUR per person.
meals.dinner: Costes Downtown — Budapest's celebrated modern European restaurant with Hungarian influences, near the Danube. Budget ~35–45 EUR per person. For a more casual option, try a traditional csárda (Hungarian tavern) in the Jewish Quarter for ~15–20 EUR.

day_by_day.notes: Széchenyi Baths entry costs ~25–30 EUR; bring or rent a towel and swimwear. Sunday is a popular day — book tickets online. The Opera House guided tour costs ~10 EUR and is highly recommended for architecture lovers.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Hungarian Parliament Building — one of Europe's most magnificent parliament buildings, with an extraordinary Neo-Gothic interior. Guided tours run regularly and include the Crown Jewels of Hungary. Book in advance online. Afterward, walk along the Danube Promenade (Duna-korzó) and visit the moving Shoes on the Danube Bank memorial — 60 pairs of iron shoes commemorating Jews shot into the river during WWII.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Jewish Quarter (VII. District) in depth. Visit the Great Synagogue on Dohány Street — the largest synagogue in Europe and second largest in the world. The complex includes the Hungarian Jewish Museum and the haunting Holocaust Memorial (Tree of Life sculpture). Wander through the ruin bar streets and the eclectic Gozsdu Courtyard.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cruise on the Danube — a 1-hour boat tour at dusk offers unparalleled views of the illuminated Parliament, Chain Bridge, and Buda Castle. Afterward, explore the trendy Kazinczy Street area for dinner and nightlife.

meals.breakfast: Café Gerbeaud on Vörösmarty Square — a legendary Budapest confectionery since 1858, famous for its Dobos cake and strudel. Budget ~10–14 EUR.
meals.lunch: Mazel Tov — a stylish Israeli-Hungarian fusion restaurant in the Jewish Quarter with an open courtyard and excellent mezze plates. Budget ~14–20 EUR per person.
meals.dinner: Mák Bisztró — a celebrated bistro offering creative Hungarian cuisine with seasonal, locally sourced ingredients in a relaxed setting. Budget ~25–35 EUR per person.

day_by_day.notes: Parliament tours must be booked online in advance — EU citizens get a significant discount. The Great Synagogue costs ~15 EUR to enter. The Danube evening cruise costs ~15–20 EUR; book through operators like Legenda or Budapest Boat.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Heroes' Square (Hősök tere) — Budapest's grandest square featuring the Millennium Monument with statues of the seven chieftains of the Magyars and Hungarian kings. Explore the adjacent Museum of Fine Arts (Szépművészeti Múzeum) — one of Central Europe's finest art museums with works by El Greco, Raphael, and Rembrandt. Stroll through the neighboring City Park (Városliget).
day_by_day.afternoon: Final souvenir shopping and cultural browsing. Visit the Central Market Hall (Nagycsarnok) for Hungarian paprika, Tokaji wine, Unicum liqueur, and handmade crafts to bring home. Take a final leisurely walk across the Chain Bridge or Liberty Bridge for last views of the Danube panorama. Pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Budapest — celebrate the end of a wonderful dual-city journey with a special meal.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or a local neighborhood café near your accommodation. Try a traditional Hungarian breakfast with lángos or kürtőskalács (chimney cake). Budget ~7–10 EUR.
meals.lunch: Stand-up lunch at the Great Market Hall — grab freshly made lángos (deep-fried dough with sour cream and cheese) and a glass of Hungarian wine from the upper-floor food stalls. Budget ~8–12 EUR.
meals.dinner: Onyx Restaurant — Budapest's flagship fine-dining destination with two Michelin stars, offering a spectacular tasting menu of modern Hungarian cuisine. A memorable splurge to close the trip. Budget ~80–120 EUR per person for the tasting menu. For a mid-range farewell: Babel Budapest (~35–50 EUR) offers a similarly creative Hungarian experience at a gentler price point.

day_by_day.notes: Check flight or train departure time and plan the day accordingly — allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for airport transfers and check-in. Budapest Liszt Ferenc Airport is ~30–40 minutes from the city center by taxi or the 100E airport bus (~3 EUR). This completes your 8-day Prague + Budapest cultural journey!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Eastern Europe (Prague + Budapest) Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Transfer — Flight LH lands at 13:00; nothing scheduled before arrival. Private luxury transfer from Václav Havel Airport to your boutique hotel in Hradčany district. Check-in, freshen up, and settle into your room with views over Prague Castle.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hradčany Neighbourhood Orientation Walk — Begin your Prague experience steps from the hotel. Stroll through Hradčany Square (Hradčanské náměstí), admire the Archbishop's Palace façade, and enter Prague Castle complex for a self-paced first look at St. Vitus Cathedral exterior and the Golden Lane. The castle grounds are walkable in under 10 minutes from most Hradčany hotels.
day_by_day.evening: Welcome Dinner in Malá Strana — Descend the castle steps into the Little Quarter for a celebratory dinner at a premium riverside restaurant. Enjoy contemporary Czech cuisine paired with Moravian wines while taking in illuminated castle views across the Vltava.

meals.breakfast: N/A — mid-day arrival
meals.lunch: Light welcome refreshments at the hotel upon check-in; alternatively grab a gourmet charcuterie board at a Hradčany wine bar near the castle gates
meals.dinner: Field Restaurant (Dlouhá 32, Old Town adjacent) or Alcron Restaurant at Radisson Blu Alcron — tasting menu with wine pairing; reserve in advance

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. Confirm early check-in with the hotel given 13:00 arrival. Keep Day 1 light — jet lag and travel fatigue are common. September weather in Prague is typically mild (15–20°C), ideal for evening strolls.

day_by_day.morning: Prague Castle Deep Dive — Return to Prague Castle complex with a premium skip-the-line guided tour. Explore St. Vitus Cathedral interior (including Royal Crypt), Old Royal Palace, St. George's Basilica, and the Story of Prague Castle exhibition. Hire a private art-history guide for an immersive 2.5-hour experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Malá Strana & Charles Bridge — Walk down to the Little Quarter, explore the baroque gardens of Wallenstein Palace, and cross the iconic Charles Bridge. Continue into Old Town (Staré Město) to visit the Astronomical Clock (Orloj) and Old Town Square. Stop at a premium café for afternoon coffee and trdelník.
day_by_day.evening: Classical Concert at Lobkowicz Palace — Attend one of the intimate evening chamber concerts held inside Lobkowicz Palace within the castle complex. The palace houses a remarkable private art collection. Follow with dinner in Old Town.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Café Savoy (Vítězná 5, Malá Strana) — Art Nouveau interiors, exceptional pastries and eggs
meals.lunch: Coda Restaurant at Aria Hotel (Tržiště 9, Malá Strana) — rooftop terrace with castle views, seasonal Czech-European menu
meals.dinner: La Degustation Bohême Bourgeoise (Haštalská 18, Old Town) — Michelin-starred, 11-course tasting menu celebrating historic Czech recipes

day_by_day.notes: Book Lobkowicz Palace concerts online well in advance — they sell out. La Degustation requires reservations weeks ahead. Comfortable walking shoes essential for cobblestones.

day_by_day.morning: Jewish Quarter (Josefov) Private Tour — Cross the river to explore the UNESCO-listed Jewish Quarter with a private historian guide. Visit the Old Jewish Cemetery, Old-New Synagogue (Europe's oldest active synagogue), Pinkas Synagogue with its haunting Holocaust memorial, and the Jewish Museum collections.
day_by_day.afternoon: Vyšehrad Citadel & Panoramic Views — Take a taxi or tram to the ancient Vyšehrad fortress on the southern bluff above the Vltava. Walk the ramparts, visit St. Peter and Paul Cathedral, and explore the Slavín Cemetery where Czech luminaries including Dvořák and Mucha are buried. Enjoy sweeping river panoramas.
day_by_day.evening: Prague Opera Night — Attend a performance at the stunning Neo-Rococo State Opera House (Státní opera Praha) or the National Theatre. Prague's opera season is in full swing in September. Choose from Czech classics — Dvořák or Smetana — or international repertoire.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Eska (Pernerova 49, Karlín district) — award-winning modern Czech bistro; fermented and foraged ingredients, excellent natural wine list
meals.dinner: Pre-theatre dinner at Augustine Restaurant in Augustine Hotel (Letenská 12, Malá Strana) — elegant setting in a restored 13th-century monastery; post-opera nightcap at a rooftop bar

day_by_day.notes: Book opera/theatre tickets online in advance. Jewish Quarter entry requires a combined ticket — purchase online to skip queues. The Josefov tour is best done in the morning before crowds build.

day_by_day.morning: Mucha Museum & Art Nouveau Prague — Visit the Alfons Mucha Museum for an intimate look at the Art Nouveau master's work. Then walk to the Municipal House (Obecní dům), a masterpiece of Czech Art Nouveau — join a guided interior tour of the Smetana Hall and ornate reception rooms.
day_by_day.afternoon: Vinohrady & Žižkov Exploration — Venture into the elegant Vinohrady neighbourhood for a different side of Prague: leafy boulevards, beautiful apartment buildings, and independent boutiques. Visit the Church of the Most Sacred Heart of Our Lord. Explore the quirky Žižkov Television Tower (with David Černý's crawling babies sculptures) for panoramic city views.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Prague Dinner & Departure Prep — Enjoy a final premium Prague dinner with a curated wine pairing. Pack and prepare for the Budapest leg of the journey.

meals.breakfast: Café Louvre (Národní 22, New Town) — historic literary café, grand Central European breakfast tradition
meals.lunch: Sansho (Petrská 25, New Town) — innovative Asian-Czech fusion using local farmers' produce; relaxed but sophisticated
meals.dinner: Manifesto Market (seasonal) or Kampa Park (Na Kampě 8b) — premium riverside terrace restaurant, European fine dining with exceptional Vltava views for a memorable Prague farewell

day_by_day.notes: Arrange luggage storage or late checkout with the hotel. Book private transfer to Praha hlavní nádraží (main train station) for the Regiojet or Railjet luxury train to Budapest the following morning. Confirm Budapest accommodation check-in time.

day_by_day.morning: Scenic Train Journey Prague → Budapest — Board the premium Railjet or Regiojet service from Praha hlavní nádraží. The journey takes approximately 6.5–7 hours through stunning Central European landscapes (Bohemia, Moravia, Slovakia). Enjoy first-class seating with table service. Arrive Budapest Keleti station early afternoon.
day_by_day.afternoon: Budapest Arrival & Buda Castle District — Private luxury transfer from Keleti to your Budapest accommodation. After check-in, take the historic Funicular (Budavári Sikló) up Castle Hill. Explore Buda Castle, the Hungarian National Gallery, and stroll along the Fisherman's Bastion for sweeping panoramas of the Danube and Pest skyline.
day_by_day.evening: Matthias Church & Castle Hill at Dusk — Watch the golden hour light transform the Matthias Church (Mátyás-templom) and the surrounding medieval streetscape. Descend to the Danube embankment for a sunset walk along the UNESCO-listed riverbank. Dinner in the Castle District.

meals.breakfast: Packed premium breakfast box arranged by Prague hotel, or first-class train café service
meals.lunch: On-board dining on the Railjet (book first-class with meal service) or packed gourmet picnic from a Prague deli
meals.dinner: Alabárdos Restaurant (Országház u. 2, Castle District) — intimate fine dining in a Gothic building; Hungarian haute cuisine with foie gras, game, and Tokaj wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: Book train tickets in advance — first-class sells out on weekends. Confirm Budapest hotel check-in flexibility. The Castle Hill funicular closes at 22:00. September in Budapest is warm (18–24°C) — perfect for evening riverside walks.

day_by_day.morning: Hungarian Parliament Building Private Tour — Cross the Chain Bridge (Széchenyi Lánchíd) to Pest and join a premium guided tour of the extraordinary neo-Gothic Hungarian Parliament, one of Europe's largest and most ornate legislative buildings. See the Hungarian Holy Crown and Crown Jewels on display.
day_by_day.afternoon: St. Stephen's Basilica & Andrássy Avenue — Visit St. Stephen's Basilica, Budapest's largest church, and ascend the dome for panoramic views. Walk the grand Andrássy Avenue — Budapest's Champs-Élysées — past its magnificent neo-Renaissance mansions to Heroes' Square (Hősök tere) and the Millennium Monument. Explore the Museum of Fine Arts.
day_by_day.evening: Budapest Opera House & Dinner — Attend a performance at the Hungarian State Opera House (Magyar Állami Operaház), one of the most beautiful opera venues in the world. Pre-performance dinner at a nearby fine dining establishment.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or New York Café (Erzsébet krt. 9–11) — the 'world's most beautiful café,' an unmissable Art Nouveau/Baroque experience with a lavish breakfast
meals.lunch: Borkonyha WineKitchen (Sas u. 3, Inner City) — Michelin-starred Hungarian wine-focused cuisine; seasonal tasting menu
meals.dinner: Costes Restaurant (Ráday u. 4, Ferencváros) — Budapest's first Michelin-starred restaurant; contemporary European tasting menu with Hungarian influences and outstanding wine cellar

day_by_day.notes: Parliament tours must be booked online in advance — the English-language tours sell out quickly on weekends. Opera tickets should be reserved weeks ahead for September performances. New York Café requires reservations for sit-down meals.

day_by_day.morning: Thermal Spa Experience — Indulge in Budapest's legendary thermal spa culture. Visit Széchenyi Thermal Bath (the largest in Europe, in a stunning neo-Baroque building) or opt for the more intimate and architecturally exquisite Gellért Thermal Bath. Book a premium private cabin and full spa treatment package.
day_by_day.afternoon: Great Market Hall & Jewish Quarter — Explore the magnificent Great Market Hall (Nagyvásárcsarnok) for gourmet Hungarian products — pick up Tokaj wine, Mangalica salami, paprika, and handcrafted souvenirs. Then walk to the Jewish Quarter: visit the Great Synagogue (Dohány Street Synagogue, Europe's largest), the Hungarian Jewish Museum, and the haunting Raoul Wallenberg Memorial Park.
day_by_day.evening: Danube River Cruise — Board a premium private or small-group dinner cruise on the Danube at sunset. Glide past illuminated landmarks: the Parliament, Chain Bridge, Buda Castle, and Gellért Hill. White-tablecloth dining with Hungarian wines aboard.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Gerbeaud (Vörösmarty tér 7, Inner City) — Budapest's most iconic café and confectionery since 1858; Hungarian pastries, cakes, and light lunch
meals.dinner: Premium Danube dinner cruise — Legenda or Silver Line private cruise with à la carte Hungarian-European menu and live music; or post-cruise dinner at Spoon The Boat restaurant

day_by_day.notes: Book Széchenyi or Gellért spa treatments in advance — massage and private cabin packages fill up. Danube dinner cruises should be reserved 2–3 days ahead. Great Synagogue is closed on Saturdays; Monday is ideal.

day_by_day.morning: Gellért Hill & Citadella — Take a morning walk or taxi up Gellért Hill for the finest panoramic views of Budapest — the entire city, both banks of the Danube, and all seven bridges spread before you. Visit the Liberty Statue (Szabadság-szobor) and the Citadella fortress. A peaceful, reflective final morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-Minute Exploration & Shopping — Return to Andrássy Avenue for luxury shopping (Hungarian design, Herend porcelain, Tokaj wines). Visit the House of Terror Museum (Terror Háza) on Andrássy Avenue for a powerful and moving account of Hungary's 20th-century history under Nazi and Soviet regimes — deeply important cultural context.
day_by_day.evening: Grand Farewell Dinner — Conclude the journey with a celebratory farewell dinner at Budapest's finest establishment. Reflect on 8 extraordinary days across two of Central Europe's greatest cities.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — take your time on the final morning
meals.lunch: Onyx Restaurant (Vörösmarty tér 7, Inner City) — Michelin two-star, the pinnacle of Hungarian fine dining; tasting menu celebrating Hungarian terroir
meals.dinner: Stand Restaurant (Széll Kálmán tér 2) — Michelin-starred, chef Tamás Széll's celebrated modern Hungarian cuisine; exceptional wine pairing with Tokaj Aszú dessert wine to close the trip

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private luxury transfer to Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport for your departure flight. Confirm transfer timing based on flight schedule — allow 2.5 hours before international departure. House of Terror is closed Mondays; Tuesday is ideal. Onyx requires advance reservation. Consider purchasing Tokaj wine and Herend porcelain as premium souvenirs — both can be packed safely with hotel assistance.
